layers.name: Data & Knowledge
layers.description: The information the AI can use: documents, databases, retrieval, context, memory and the systems that keep that information current.

layers.name: Model
layers.description: The model that performs language, reasoning, coding, vision or audio tasks. This is the raw capability layer.

layers.name: Agent & Infrastructure
layers.description: The runtime around the model: tools, state, memory, orchestration, permissions, sandboxes and the ability to take actions.

layers.name: Application & Workflow
layers.description: The user experience and business process where AI is used, from copilots to end-to-end task flows.

layers.name: Production & Business
layers.description: Everything needed to run AI responsibly at scale: evals, monitoring, governance, cost, risk, reliability and measurable business value.

primitives.name: Compute
primitives.description: Where it runs. This covers model inference, agent runtimes, application code, indexing, evals and other processing.

primitives.name: Networking
primitives.description: How it connects. This covers traffic between users, models, tools, data sources, APIs and enterprise systems.

primitives.name: Storage
primitives.description: Where data and state live. This includes documents, databases, vectors, memory, logs, traces and application state.

primitives.name: Security
primitives.description: Who or what is allowed access. This includes identity, permissions, secrets, isolation, approvals and audit controls.

impacts.name: Disruptive
impacts.description: Changes what is practical to build or reshapes the market enough that old assumptions need to be reconsidered.

impacts.name: Step-change
impacts.description: A clear jump in capability, cost, reliability or usability that changes architecture decisions, but does not reset the whole market.

impacts.name: Incremental
impacts.description: A meaningful improvement to an existing approach. It matters, but the basic architecture and workflow stay mostly the same.

impacts.name: Packaging / distribution
impacts.description: The underlying capability mostly existed already, but it becomes easier, cheaper, more integrated or available to more teams.

trajectories.description: Getting the right information into the system.
trajectories.now: Long context, retrieval, connected company data, citations, and memory are increasingly combined.
trajectories.direction: Permission-aware organizational context that stays fresh and can be reused across models and agents.
trajectories.constraint: Freshness, provenance, permissions, data quality, and cost.

trajectories.now: Frontier models reason longer, operate computers, work across modalities, and improve rapidly on professional tasks.
trajectories.direction: Broader, more general capability with adaptive reasoning and model routing by task, cost, latency, and risk.
trajectories.constraint: Alignment, inference cost, reliability, misuse risk, and knowing when capability is actually trustworthy.

trajectories.description: Turning model capability into sustained action.
trajectories.now: Managed runtimes, tools, MCP, subagents, computer use, state, and tracing support longer tasks.
trajectories.direction: Persistent software actors that can work for hours or days, recover from failure, coordinate, and operate across systems.
trajectories.constraint: Long-horizon reliability, identity, bounded permissions, verification, and recovery.

trajectories.description: Where AI changes how work is actually done.
trajectories.now: The pattern is moving from assistance beside the workflow to agents executing meaningful parts of the workflow.
trajectories.direction: AI-native processes where machines execute routine and analytical work while people handle goals, judgment, approvals, and exceptions.
trajectories.constraint: Workflow redesign, adoption, accountability, process ownership, and proving business value.

trajectories.description: Making AI controllable, measurable, and economically useful. LLMOps and GenAIOps practices for running GenAI in production grew gradually from 2023 onward.
trajectories.now: Evals, traces, trajectory monitoring, governance, approval gates, and cost controls are becoming core production architecture.
trajectories.direction: Continuous risk-based control where capability, alignment, reliability, cost, and business value are measured together.
trajectories.constraint: Scalable alignment and oversight as models become more capable and autonomous.

updates.title: OpenAI releases ChatGPT as a public research preview
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI released ChatGPT as a free research preview. People could talk to a language model in plain conversation and ask follow-up questions.
updates.whyCare: Chat became the way most people first used a language model.
updates.before: People used language models mainly through research demos, APIs and specialist tools.
updates.after: Anyone with a browser could use a capable model through a chat window.
updates.learn: Treat chat as one interface among several. Keep the conversation layer separate from the model and the business logic behind it.

sources.name: OpenAI - Introducing ChatGPT

updates.architectureImplication: Design the chat interface, the model and the business workflow as separate layers, so each can change on its own.

updates.title: OpenAI releases GPT-4, which accepts both images and text
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI released GPT-4, a large multimodal model that accepts image and text input. It improved on professional and academic benchmarks.
updates.whyCare: Harder knowledge work and image-plus-text use cases became realistic, and so did the need for evaluation and controls.
updates.before: Most GenAI applications ran on weaker, text-only models.
updates.after: Teams could build for more complex reasoning, higher-stakes workflows and image-plus-text input.
updates.learn: Test the model on your own tasks before you raise the stakes. Add evaluation and controls as capability grows.

sources.name: OpenAI - GPT-4 research
OpenAI - GPT-4

updates.architectureImplication: A stronger model still needs evaluations, good data, controls and workflow design around it.

updates.title: OpenAI adds function calling so models can return structured tool calls
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI added function calling to its API. A model can pick a described function and return structured arguments that code can use to call an API or tool.
updates.whyCare: Applications could let models trigger software actions reliably.
updates.before: Developers parsed free text or relied on fragile prompt conventions to connect models to software.
updates.after: Models return structured tool calls that code can validate and run.
updates.learn: Let the model choose the action and let your code run it. Check arguments and permissions before any tool runs.

sources.name: OpenAI - Function calling and other API updates

updates.architectureImplication: Separate model judgment from deterministic execution. Put validation and permission checks between them.

updates.title: Google previews Gemini 1.5 Pro with a one-million-token context window
updates.whatChanged: Google introduced Gemini 1.5 Pro with a standard 128,000-token context window. A one-million-token window was available in private preview for selected developers and enterprise customers.
updates.whyCare: Very long context changed the choice between retrieval and putting source material straight into the prompt.
updates.before: Teams split large document sets into small chunks and retrieved a few at a time.
updates.after: Some workloads could send far larger collections directly. Retrieval still mattered for cost, freshness, permissions and precision.
updates.learn: Test long context, retrieval and a mix of both on your data. Compare cost, latency and accuracy.

sources.name: Google - Introducing Gemini 1.5

updates.architectureImplication: Choose between long context, retrieval or both based on data size, freshness, latency, cost and access control.

updates.title: OpenAI releases GPT-4o, one model for text, vision and audio
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI introduced GPT-4o, trained as a single model across text, vision and audio. It can respond to audio input in as little as 232 milliseconds.
updates.whyCare: Voice and multimodal products need fewer separate speech, vision and language components.
updates.before: Voice applications chained several models and conversion steps.
updates.after: One model can handle more of the interaction directly.
updates.learn: For voice and multimodal products, plan for streaming, interruptions, session state and cost.

sources.name: OpenAI - Hello GPT-4o

updates.architectureImplication: Design multimodal systems around streaming, latency, session state and interruption handling.

updates.title: Meta releases Llama 3.1, including an openly available 405B model
updates.whatChanged: Meta released Llama 3.1, including a 405B model with a 128K context window. The weights are available for broad use under Meta's license.
updates.whyCare: Teams could run a model close to the frontier on infrastructure they control.
updates.before: Frontier-level capability sat mostly behind closed, hosted APIs.
updates.after: Enterprises had a strong open-weight option for control, customization and deployment.
updates.learn: Compare licensing, data location, hosting cost and the skills you need to run it before you self-host.

sources.name: Meta - Introducing Llama 3.1

updates.architectureImplication: Weigh who runs the model, the license and the effort to operate it, next to quality and price.

updates.title: OpenAI releases o1, a model that reasons before it answers
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI released o1-preview, a model series that spends more time reasoning before responding. It improves on harder science, coding and math tasks.
updates.whyCare: Reasoning time became a setting you choose, with a trade-off between quality, latency and cost.
updates.before: Teams treated most model calls as the same kind of single-pass answer.
updates.after: Teams can choose when a task is worth more reasoning time and cost.
updates.learn: Route tasks by difficulty and value. Save expensive reasoning for the tasks that need it.

sources.name: OpenAI - Introducing o1-preview

updates.architectureImplication: Add routing between fast and reasoning models, based on task difficulty, risk and cost.

updates.title: Anthropic releases computer use, letting Claude operate graphical software
updates.whatChanged: Anthropic released computer use in public beta. Claude can look at screenshots, move a pointer, click and type through software interfaces.
updates.whyCare: Agents can act in systems that have no API, though reliability and security remain hard.
updates.before: Automation needed APIs, scripts or fragile browser automation.
updates.after: A model can operate existing graphical software in a general way.
updates.learn: Run computer-use agents in a sandbox. Limit credentials and plan how to check and undo their actions.

sources.name: Anthropic - Developing a computer use model

updates.architectureImplication: Computer use widens what agents can reach. Add sandboxing, credential limits, verification and recovery.

updates.title: Anthropic open-sources MCP, a standard for connecting AI to tools and data
updates.whatChanged: Anthropic open-sourced the Model Context Protocol, a standard way to connect AI assistants to data sources, business tools and development environments.
updates.whyCare: Teams can build a connector once and use it with many AI clients.
updates.before: Each application or framework needed its own connection to each tool and data source.
updates.after: Tools and data sources can expose one interface that many AI clients use.
updates.learn: Check which of your tools already offer MCP servers. Adopt a protocol once the ecosystem around it grows.

sources.name: Anthropic - Introducing the Model Context Protocol

updates.architectureImplication: Use a shared protocol for tool and data connections to reduce coupling between AI clients and systems.

updates.title: DeepSeek releases R1, an open-weight reasoning model with low API prices
updates.whatChanged: DeepSeek released R1 and smaller distilled reasoning models with open weights under the MIT license. API prices were $0.14 to $0.55 per million input tokens and $2.19 per million output tokens.
updates.whyCare: Reasoning became available at lower cost and with open weights, which put pressure on closed-model prices.
updates.before: Advanced reasoning came mainly from a few closed providers.
updates.after: Teams had more choice across quality, hosting control, openness and cost.
updates.learn: Keep your design portable across providers. Test new models quickly when capability and prices move.

sources.name: DeepSeek - R1 release

updates.architectureImplication: Avoid tying the architecture to one provider. Model routing and portability gain value as prices change.

updates.title: OpenAI launches the Responses API, built-in tools and an Agents SDK
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI released the Responses API, built-in tools for web search, file search and computer use, and an Agents SDK with tracing.
updates.whyCare: Teams could buy core agent infrastructure as a managed service and write less orchestration code.
updates.before: Teams assembled tool use, orchestration, tracing and state with custom code or separate frameworks.
updates.after: More of the agent harness comes from the platform.
updates.learn: Decide which parts of the agent harness to buy and which to build. Check what you can export or move later.

sources.name: OpenAI - New tools for building agents

updates.architectureImplication: Managed agent runtimes change build-versus-buy decisions. Weigh speed of delivery against portability.

updates.title: Google announces A2A, a protocol for agents to work with other agents
updates.whatChanged: Google announced the Agent2Agent protocol so agents from different vendors and frameworks can communicate and coordinate.
updates.whyCare: Agent-to-agent interoperability became a stated industry goal. Standards still need adoption before teams can rely on them.
updates.before: Multi-agent systems assumed one framework, one vendor or custom conventions.
updates.after: A shared protocol could reduce coupling between agent systems as adoption grows.
updates.learn: Track which vendors support A2A. Adopt it when your partners or customers need cross-vendor agents.

sources.name: Google - Announcing the Agent2Agent Protocol

updates.architectureImplication: Plan agent boundaries so a standard protocol can replace custom connections later.

updates.title: OpenAI adds remote MCP servers and background mode to the Responses API
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI added support for remote MCP servers, a background mode for long-running tasks, and further reliability and privacy features to its Responses API.
updates.whyCare: Managed runtimes now handle more of the connections and long-running execution that agents need.
updates.before: Teams built connectivity and long-running execution for agents themselves.
updates.after: The platform covers more of the operational agent harness.
updates.learn: Check what the managed runtime lets you see, export and secure. Decide how much lock-in you accept for the convenience.

sources.name: OpenAI - New tools and features in the Responses API

updates.architectureImplication: Managed runtimes can absorb connectivity and long-running work. Keep observability and an exit path in your design.

updates.title: Long-running agent reliability is becoming the real bottleneck
updates.whatChanged: Frontier agent systems can already execute multi-step work, but reliability falls as tasks get longer and tool use becomes more complex. The engineering focus is shifting toward state, recovery, verification and trajectory-level control.
updates.whyCare: For enterprise architecture, the question is moving from whether an agent can do one task to whether it can complete a long workflow safely and repeatedly.
updates.before: Agents were judged mainly on impressive individual tasks and demos.
updates.after: Architecture increasingly centers on reliable execution across many steps, tools, failures and approvals.
updates.learn: Long-horizon reliability, persistent state, retries, recovery, verification and human escalation.

sources.name: Microsoft Research - long-horizon tasks

updates.architectureImplication: Long-horizon reliability, persistent state, retries, recovery, verification and human escalation.

updates.title: Agent security is moving from app security to actor-level control
updates.whatChanged: As agents gain tools and autonomy, enterprises increasingly need agent identity, scoped permissions, sandboxing, audit logs and approval gates.
updates.whyCare: An agent with access to enterprise systems behaves more like a software actor than a chatbot. It needs its own operating controls.
updates.before: Secure the AI application and its API access.
updates.after: Secure each agent as an actor with identity, privileges and auditable actions.
updates.learn: Least privilege, credential isolation, agent identity, sandboxing and approval gates.

sources.name: Google Cloud - workload identities

updates.architectureImplication: Least privilege, credential isolation, agent identity, sandboxing and approval gates.

updates.title: Managed agent runtimes continue to reduce custom harness work
updates.whatChanged: More providers are packaging context, tools, subagents, execution and long-running task infrastructure into managed agent runtimes.
updates.whyCare: The underlying patterns already existed, but lower implementation friction changes build-versus-buy decisions.
updates.before: Teams assembled much of the harness themselves or through separate frameworks.
updates.after: More runtime pieces can be consumed as managed infrastructure.
updates.learn: Agent harness means state, context, tools, execution, retries, permissions, memory and observability.

sources.name: OpenAI - agent platform reference

updates.architectureImplication: Agent harness means state, context, tools, execution, retries, permissions, memory and observability.

updates.title: Teams start to evaluate the path an agent takes as well as its answer
updates.whatChanged: Teams now need to check which tools an agent used, which path it took and whether it stayed inside policy. Checking the final answer alone misses these.
updates.whyCare: A correct-looking answer can come from an unsafe path. This matters once agents take actions.
updates.before: Teams evaluated whether the final answer was correct.
updates.after: Teams evaluate the result and the sequence of actions that produced it.
updates.learn: Add trajectory checks to your evaluations. Keep audit logs and use human review for risky actions.

sources.name: Microsoft Research - diagnosing agent failures

updates.architectureImplication: Combine output evaluations, trajectory evaluations, audit logs, policy checks and risk-based human review.

updates.title: Enterprise agent building, governance, and scale became a single platform concern
updates.whatChanged: Google Cloud Next 2026 introduced an end-to-end enterprise agent platform spanning agent building, governance, and scale.
updates.whyCare: Agent infrastructure is becoming a first-class cloud platform category rather than a collection of disconnected components.
updates.before: Teams stitched together models, tools, orchestration, identity, and governance across separate services.
updates.after: Cloud platforms increasingly package those concerns into integrated agent platforms.
updates.learn: Compare integrated agent platforms on portability, observability, governance, cost, and ecosystem fit.

sources.name: Google Cloud Next 2026 recap

updates.architectureImplication: Compare integrated agent platforms on portability, observability, governance, cost, and ecosystem fit.

updates.title: Google announces Gemini Spark, a persistent agent across Workspace apps
updates.whatChanged: Google announced Gemini Spark, a persistent personal agent that acts across Workspace applications under user direction.
updates.whyCare: AI at work is moving from a chat tool next to the work to an agent inside the software people already use.
updates.before: AI helped in single prompts or inside one application at a time.
updates.after: A persistent agent can coordinate work across several everyday applications.
updates.learn: Define what users may delegate, which actions need approval and what context the agent may see.

sources.name: Google Workspace updates 2026

updates.architectureImplication: Design for delegation, approvals, context boundaries and user control when agents act across applications.

updates.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5, built for long and complex tasks
updates.whatChanged: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5. Anthropic says its lead over its other models grows with the length and complexity of the task, across coding, knowledge work, vision and research.
updates.whyCare: How long and complex a task a model can finish is becoming a main way to compare models.
updates.before: Hard tasks had to be split into many small steps with a person checking each one.
updates.after: Stronger models can carry larger projects further before handing control back.
updates.learn: Test models on how long and how complex a task they finish reliably. Use your own tasks.

sources.name: Anthropic - Claude Fable 5

updates.architectureImplication: Evaluate models on task length and complexity as well as benchmark scores.

updates.title: OpenAI moves safety evaluation from single actions to whole trajectories
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI reported new failure types during limited internal use of a long-running model. It responded with new evaluations, long-horizon alignment work, trajectory monitoring and more user control.
updates.whyCare: Once systems act over long periods, checking single outputs misses what the sequence of actions is working toward.
updates.before: Safety checks focused on single responses or short, bounded tasks.
updates.after: Teams need to judge whole sequences of actions and step in during a run.
updates.learn: Add trajectory monitoring, long-horizon evaluations, approval points and recovery steps to agent designs.

sources.name: OpenAI - Safety and alignment in an era of long-horizon models

updates.architectureImplication: Monitor whole agent runs. Define where a run must stop for approval and how to recover it.

updates.title: Enterprise AI is moving from assistance toward execution inside real workflows
updates.whatChanged: Published enterprise examples increasingly show agents connected to tools and company context for onboarding, account management, developer work, and other multi-step processes.
updates.whyCare: The important application shift is not a better chatbot. It is delegation of substantive parts of a business process.
updates.before: AI mostly assisted people with drafting, search, and isolated tasks beside the workflow.
updates.after: Leading teams increasingly connect agents to context and tools and make successful workflows repeatable.
updates.learn: Start workflow design with task boundaries, data, tools, approvals, failure handling, and measurable outcome.

sources.name: OpenAI - AI-native company workflows

updates.architectureImplication: Start workflow design with task boundaries, data, tools, approvals, failure handling, and measurable outcome.

updates.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Astra with gains in computer use, science and cyber
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra and reported state-of-the-art results on benchmarks for computer use, science, cybersecurity and professional work.
updates.whyCare: Frontier models now operate software and carry out complex professional tasks as well as answering questions.
updates.before: Models were less reliable at long, tool-using professional work and computer use.
updates.after: A frontier model handles a wider set of complex tasks and operates software better.
updates.learn: Test it on your own tool-using tasks. Treat vendor benchmark results as claims until you reproduce them.

sources.name: OpenAI - GPT-6 Astra
OpenAI - GPT-6 Astra safety overview

updates.architectureImplication: Broader capability needs stronger controls, routing, monitoring and risk assessment around the model.
updates.verificationNote: The OpenAI page shows only a 29 September 2026 update. Launch date confirmed by news coverage.

updates.title: Automated research moved from aspiration to an internal working milestone
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI said coding agents were accelerating internal research and that it had reached its goal of an automated research intern working under human supervision.
updates.whyCare: Automating parts of AI research itself is a directional signal toward agents that improve the speed of capability and alignment research.
updates.before: AI systems mainly assisted researchers on bounded tasks.
updates.after: Research agents can take on larger experiment and implementation loops under supervision.
updates.learn: Watch research automation because it can accelerate both model progress and the need for alignment and governance.

sources.name: OpenAI - Research acceleration

updates.architectureImplication: Watch research automation because it can accelerate both model progress and the need for alignment and governance.

updates.title: Business data, analysis, dashboards, and action are converging into one agent workflow
updates.whatChanged: A business data agent combined connected company data, investigation, analysis, and interactive dashboards in one workflow.
updates.whyCare: It packages retrieval, business context, analysis, and reporting into a simpler experience for non-specialists.
updates.before: Business users often waited for analysts or moved manually between BI tools, SQL, spreadsheets, and reports.
updates.after: A conversational agent can investigate connected business data and create shareable analysis directly.
updates.learn: The architectural issues move to data permissions, metric definitions, provenance, freshness, and auditability.

sources.name: OpenAI - Now everyone can put data to work

updates.architectureImplication: The architectural issues move to data permissions, metric definitions, provenance, freshness, and auditability.

updates.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for financial services with premium market data
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI launched a financial-services edition of ChatGPT. It combines premium market data from partners such as Daloopa and PitchBook with GPT-6 Astra for research, modeling and client materials.
updates.whyCare: AI products are becoming industry-specific, with data rights and workflows built in.
updates.before: Teams combined a general assistant, data subscriptions, templates and controls themselves.
updates.after: A vertical product packages trusted data, domain workflows, output formats and governance together.
updates.learn: When you compare vertical AI products, check data rights, workflow fit and governance as closely as the model.

sources.name: OpenAI - ChatGPT for Financial Services

updates.architectureImplication: Expect more industry products where data rights and workflow design matter as much as the model.

updates.title: Research finds AI use adds new recurring tasks to people's jobs
updates.whatChanged: Economic research reported that some AI-assisted tasks outside a worker's usual occupation become recurring parts of their work.
updates.whyCare: AI may change what jobs include as well as how fast people work.
updates.before: Teams measured AI adoption as faster work on the same tasks.
updates.after: Some workers add new recurring tasks because AI lowers the skill or effort needed.
updates.learn: Measure changes in tasks and roles alongside time saved.

sources.name: OpenAI - How workers are unlocking new ways of working

updates.architectureImplication: Measure workflow change, task expansion and role redesign alongside time savings.

updates.title: Agent runtimes are becoming more elastic for long-running and bursty agents
updates.whatChanged: AWS introduced AgentCore Runtime V2 with memory reclamation during sessions and snapshot-based startup. AWS measured about 2-second P75 cold starts across container images from 200 MB to 2 GB, versus roughly 5.4 to 30 seconds for the earlier runtime.
updates.whyCare: Production agents increasingly need isolated compute that can sit idle, resume quickly, run for long periods, and avoid paying for peak memory throughout a session.
updates.before: Teams often kept agent environments warm, paid for memory held at the session high-water mark, or built their own lifecycle machinery to reduce cold starts and idle cost.
updates.after: A managed agent runtime can scale to zero, reclaim unused memory during a session, and restore prepared environments from snapshots with more predictable startup.
updates.learn: Separate the agent harness from the agent runtime. The harness manages reasoning, tools and context; the runtime provides compute, isolation, state and lifecycle.
updates.architectureImplication: Treat agent execution as its own infrastructure layer and compare managed runtimes on isolation, startup latency, session lifecycle, state, identity, portability and cost.

sources.name: AWS - The new AgentCore runtime
AWS - AgentCore Runtime V2 documentation

updates.title: Inference-aware routing is becoming a managed production primitive
updates.whatChanged: AWS introduced SageMaker HyperPod Inference Gateway, which routes LLM requests using signals such as KV-cache utilization, queue depth, LoRA adapter residency, prefix-cache hit rate and running requests. AWS reports up to 82% lower time-to-first-token in its tests.
updates.whyCare: LLM replicas are not interchangeable in the way ordinary stateless web servers are. Cache state, queues and loaded adapters can materially change latency and GPU efficiency.
updates.before: Generic round-robin or least-connections routing could send a request to a model pod with a poor cache state, a deep queue or the wrong adapter loaded.
updates.after: An inference-aware router can select a backend using model-serving state, improving cache reuse, latency and GPU utilization without changing application clients.
updates.learn: Understand KV cache, prefix caching, time-to-first-token, prefill versus decode, LoRA adapters and inference-aware routing. These increasingly determine self-hosted model economics.
updates.architectureImplication: For dedicated GPU inference, treat routing and cache topology as part of model-serving architecture rather than using a generic load balancer by default.

sources.name: AWS - Introducing SageMaker HyperPod Inference Gateway
AWS - HyperPod Inference release notes

updates.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Sol and Luna as lower-cost model tiers
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and Luna on 22 September. Per million tokens, Sol costs $2 input and $10 output, and Luna $0.10 input and $0.50 output. OpenAI says they bring GPT-6 Astra advances to cheaper tiers.
updates.whyCare: More reasoning, coding and agent subtasks may become affordable at high volume. Compare task success, latency and total cost with retries included.
updates.before: Teams kept strong models for hard steps and used older, cheaper models for high-volume steps.
updates.after: Teams can test newer, cheaper tiers for both hard and high-volume steps.
updates.learn: Build task-specific evaluations. Route by accuracy, latency, cache hit rate, retries and cost per successful task.
updates.architectureImplication: Benchmark several models and route by workload and risk. Keep a provider abstraction and a fallback.

sources.name: OpenAI - Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna
OpenAI API changelog
OpenAI API pricing

updates.title: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 5.5 at lower prices than Opus 5
updates.whatChanged: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 on 22 September at $4 input and $20 output per million tokens, with cache reads at $0.20. Anthropic reports typical workloads cost 40% less than on Opus 5. It has a 1M-token context window and always-on adaptive thinking.
updates.whyCare: Agents that reread cached context often may cost less to run. Upgrades need testing because several thinking and tool-use behaviours changed.
updates.before: Opus 5 had higher token and cache-read prices, and existing integrations could assume optional thinking or forced tool use.
updates.after: Opus 5.5 offers cheaper cached context and faster output, according to Anthropic. Integrations need checks for always-on thinking and tool-use changes.
updates.learn: Measure total agent cost and cache hit rate on your own tasks. Run migration tests for thinking and tool-use behaviour.
updates.architectureImplication: Test Opus 5.5 on representative agent tasks and run migration tests for thinking/tool-use behavior before changing production model routing.

sources.name: Anthropic - Claude Opus 5.5 announcement
Anthropic - Opus 5.5 platform docs

updates.title: Enterprise AI is shifting from seat licensing toward measured agent work
updates.whatChanged: Microsoft described an enterprise AI operating model that combines multi-model choice, organizational data and context, centralized monitoring/governance, continuous agent improvement loops, and separate economics for human subscriptions versus autonomous agent work. The individual components already existed, but their convergence into a mainstream enterprise operating model is consequential.
updates.whyCare: As agents perform variable amounts of work, a flat per-user software price no longer describes the full economics. Architecture and product teams increasingly need to measure cost and quality per completed task or workflow, while keeping models portable and agents governed.
updates.before: Enterprise AI was often bought and managed mainly as a per-user copilot subscription, with agent cost, evaluation and governance handled separately or experimentally.
updates.after: Enterprises are increasingly treating agents as metered workloads: choose among models, ground them in enterprise context, monitor and govern them centrally, continuously evaluate outcomes, and manage variable consumption economics.
updates.learn: Understand cost per successful task, model routing, agent evaluation loops, centralized governance and the difference between predictable human-seat pricing and variable autonomous-work consumption.
updates.architectureImplication: Design enterprise agent platforms with model portability, usage and outcome telemetry, evaluation loops, policy controls and cost attribution at the workflow or agent level rather than assuming one model and one flat license.

sources.name: Microsoft - Building the system for AI at work

updates.title: Cross-platform agent governance is becoming a standalone enterprise control layer
updates.whatChanged: Dataiku launched Agent Management as a standalone product that discovers and inventories agents across major vendor platforms and custom OpenTelemetry environments, monitors health, usage, cost, quality and behavior, and maintains risk/certification evidence. The underlying monitoring and governance concepts already existed; the notable change is packaging them as a vendor-agnostic layer above fragmented agent stacks.
updates.whyCare: Enterprises adopting agents across multiple clouds and SaaS platforms need portfolio-level visibility that no single agent platform naturally provides. Governance is moving from controls inside each builder/runtime toward an independent inventory, evaluation and risk layer.
updates.before: Teams typically monitored and governed agents inside the platform where each agent was built, leaving cross-platform inventory, ownership, cost, quality and risk fragmented.
updates.after: A separate management layer can discover heterogeneous agents, map their models and tools, track operational and business measures, and maintain risk/certification evidence across platforms.
updates.learn: Understand agent inventory, OpenTelemetry-based observability, lifecycle governance, certification, business-value measurement and why multi-vendor agent estates create a control-plane problem.
updates.architectureImplication: For enterprises with agents across several platforms, consider a governance/control plane above individual runtimes rather than assuming each vendor's native monitoring provides an enterprise-wide view.

sources.name: Dataiku - Agent Management general availability announcement
Dataiku - Discover Agent Management

updates.title: Postman shows how it limits tools and context for its production agent
updates.whatChanged: Postman and AWS described Agent Mode's design. A root agent narrows over 170 tools to about 15 per task. Schema-aware queries replace many read tools, and context handlers supply relevant state. State-changing actions still need approval. Tool-selection errors rose above about 40 visible tools in Postman's testing.
updates.whyCare: Past a point, more tools and prompt text make agents less reliable. Shaping context and limiting actions keeps them working.
updates.before: Early versions used many small tools and UI-shaped data, which raised errors and latency.
updates.after: Tools are chosen per task, reads use schema-aware queries, and approvals gate changes.
updates.learn: Count your tool catalog as part of the context budget. Select tools per task and keep approval for important writes.

sources.name: AWS - How Postman runs Agent Mode for 40 million developers on Amazon Bedrock

updates.architectureImplication: Give each task a small, relevant tool set and curated context. Keep write approvals, data retention and inference region explicit.

updates.title: Ai2 replaces GPU priorities with time budgets and preemption contracts
updates.whatChanged: Ai2 replaced its priority-based GPU scheduler with fair-share allocation weighted by GPU-time budgets, plus minimum-runtime contracts that let resumable jobs be preempted. In 30 days it delivered 98% of allocated GPU hours at 98% occupancy. Debug-job p90 waits fell from two hours to 30 seconds.
updates.whyCare: Scarce GPUs tempt teams to hold capacity and inflate priorities. Budgets align use with company priorities and let idle capacity be borrowed.
updates.before: Non-preemptible jobs could hold capacity, priorities inflated, and fixed team allocations left GPUs idle.
updates.after: GPU time is shared across projects by budget, and resumable work can be preempted after a guaranteed run time.
updates.learn: Budget GPU time per team. Pair fair share with checkpointing, preemption rules and visible usage data.

sources.name: Hugging Face - Impactful scheduling for GPU clusters (Ai2)

updates.architectureImplication: Shared GPU fleets can use budget-weighted fair share with preemption. Test checkpointing and fragmentation before rollout.

updates.title: GitHub brings Claude Haiku 5.5 to all Copilot plans and surfaces
updates.whatChanged: GitHub made Claude Haiku 5.5 generally available in Copilot for individual, Business and Enterprise plans, across IDEs, Copilot CLI, cloud agent and github.com. GitHub positions it for fast, high-volume work such as subagents and quick edits. Usage is billed at provider list price.
updates.whyCare: Teams get a small, fast model for high-volume subtasks inside their existing coding tools.
updates.before: Teams had fewer integrated options for a fast model for subagents and routine coding steps.
updates.after: Organizations can enable Haiku 5.5 across Copilot under their model policies.
updates.learn: Test it on your coding and subagent tasks. Compare success rate, latency, retries and cost per finished task.

sources.name: GitHub Changelog - Claude Haiku 5.5 in GitHub Copilot

updates.architectureImplication: Add Haiku 5.5 as a routing option for short, high-volume tasks. Measure cost per successful task.

updates.title: Google announces a Gemini agent with its own identity for workplace tasks
updates.whatChanged: At Gemini at Work 2026, Google announced a Gemini agent that works across Workspace and connected systems. Team agents get their own accounts and identities, and their access follows existing sharing permissions. Google also described audit trails, sandboxed execution, model routing and spend caps.
updates.whyCare: Agent identity, permissions, audit and cost limits now come packaged in a workplace suite.
updates.before: Enterprises combined chat assistants with separate automations, and handled identity, audit and cost controls in different services.
updates.after: Team agents have their own identities, inherit access from shared resources and run under central controls.
updates.learn: Test agent-owned identity and user-delegated access on one bounded workflow. Check audit trails and spend limits.

sources.name: Google Cloud - Welcome to Gemini at Work 2026
Google - Google Cloud introduces the Gemini agent

updates.architectureImplication: Compare suite-native agents with custom agent stacks on identity, permissions, audit and lock-in. Check availability first.

tests.datedEvent: Google announced it at Gemini at Work on 8 October 2026.
tests.primarySource: Google Cloud blog and Google blog posts of 8 October 2026.
tests.designChoice: Gives agents their own identity and permissions, separate from the user who delegates to them.
tests.firstOrDefining: Qualifies if other major vendors also give agents their own identities, or if this becomes generally available and widely used.

updates.title: GitHub makes local sandboxing generally available for Copilot coding agents
updates.whatChanged: GitHub made local sandboxing generally available at no extra cost in Copilot CLI, the Copilot app and VS Code Agent Host sessions. It limits agent commands' access to files, networks and credentials. Enterprise settings can require it.
updates.whyCare: Coding agents run commands with the developer's privileges. A built-in sandbox makes limiting that access simpler.
updates.before: Copilot CLI commands ran with the user's full access unless teams added other controls.
updates.after: Organizations can turn on OS-level sandboxing across several Copilot surfaces and enforce it centrally.
updates.learn: Test the sandbox's file, network and credential limits on each operating system. Use cloud sandboxes where you need stronger isolation.

sources.name: GitHub Changelog - GitHub Copilot weekly releases, October 5
GitHub Docs - About cloud and local sandboxes for GitHub Copilot

updates.architectureImplication: Compare local sandboxing with containers, VMs and GitHub's cloud sandbox. Match the isolation level to your threat model.

updates.title: GitHub adds managed model defaults and MCP startup controls to Copilot for JetBrains
updates.whatChanged: GitHub added enterprise settings to choose the default Copilot agent model for new JetBrains conversations. Users can still pick another model. A new setting can stop configured MCP servers from starting automatically.
updates.whyCare: Administrators get a consistent starting model, and developers control when tools become active. Neither setting restricts which models or MCP tools are allowed.
updates.before: JetBrains users chose models with no managed default, and MCP servers started automatically.
updates.after: Administrators set the default model, and users can turn off automatic MCP startup.
updates.learn: Use model allowlists or a gateway where you must restrict models. Keep MCP permissions and least privilege separate from startup settings.

sources.name: GitHub Changelog - New controls and chat improvements in Copilot for JetBrains

updates.architectureImplication: Treat the default model as a preference. Enforce model policy and MCP permissions through separate controls.

updates.title: AgentCore shifted short-term agent memory to consumption-based pricing
updates.whatChanged: AWS replaced AgentCore Memory short-term memory's flat per-event price with separate ingestion, retrieval, and storage charges: $1.00/GB ingested, $0.20/GB retrieved, and $0.10/GB-month stored. Ingestion and retrieval have a 12 KB minimum and 64 KB maximum billable size per event; storage is billed on actual event size. Long-term memory pricing is unchanged.
updates.whyCare: Agent memory costs now depend more directly on event payload size, retrieval volume, and retention. Teams should include these variables in agent unit economics instead of estimating cost from event counts alone.
updates.before: Short-term memory was charged at a flat rate per event, regardless of the amount of data ingested, retrieved, or stored.
updates.after: Short-term memory has distinct data-volume charges, with minimum and maximum billable sizes for ingestion and retrieval and TTL-sensitive storage costs.
updates.learn: Model memory costs using payload distributions, retrieval frequency, and TTL; compare managed memory with alternatives using total workload cost rather than headline rates alone.

sources.name: AWS - Consumption-based pricing for short-term memory in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
AWS - Amazon Bedrock AgentCore pricing

updates.architectureImplication: Treat short-term memory payload sizing, retrieval patterns, and TTL as explicit cost and retention controls in agent design.

updates.title: GitHub adds identity attribution and per-category telemetry controls to Copilot
updates.whatChanged: GitHub added an opt-in setting that records the Copilot account, OS account and host name in OpenTelemetry data. Enterprise settings separately control capture of prompts, responses, tool arguments, tool output and policy details. All capture is off by default.
updates.whyCare: Enterprises can link agent activity to users and devices without collecting conversation content.
updates.before: Telemetry used a pseudonymous user ID, and one setting controlled all content capture.
updates.after: Administrators control identity capture and five content types separately, all off by default.
updates.learn: Collect the minimum data you need. Content capture can include source code, tool data and local paths.

sources.name: GitHub Changelog - Client telemetry user attribution and configurable capture
GitHub Docs - Enterprise managed settings

updates.architectureImplication: Keep identity and content telemetry as separate policy decisions, set centrally.

updates.title: AWS launches Lambda Web Functions for HTTP servers and streaming AI endpoints
updates.whatChanged: AWS introduced Lambda Web Functions, which run standard Node.js HTTP servers, including streaming inference endpoints. One warm environment serves up to 128 concurrent requests. Compute is billed on active CPU time and memory for the environment's lifetime. It launches on Node.js 24, Arm64 and five Regions.
updates.whyCare: Teams can deploy an HTTP server without rewriting it as an event handler, and pay less for CPU while waiting on I/O.
updates.before: Lambda required an event-handler model, so HTTP apps needed adapters or separate hosting.
updates.after: A Node.js HTTP server runs on Lambda with concurrency, native streaming and active-CPU billing.
updates.learn: Compare it with event-driven functions and containers on concurrency, memory cost, runtime and Region limits.

sources.name: AWS News Blog - Announcing AWS Lambda Web Functions
AWS What's New - AWS Lambda announces Lambda Web Functions

updates.architectureImplication: Consider HTTP-native serverless hosting for streaming inference APIs with long I/O waits.

updates.title: Gemini 4 Argon adds a frontier model focused on complex reasoning
updates.whatChanged: Google announced Gemini 4 Argon as its latest frontier model, making it available to developers and enterprises. The announcement describes visual-semantic reasoning, physical understanding, and autonomous code generation; Google reports an 87% score on its Embodied Reasoning benchmark and an internal video-to-simulation-to-robot demonstration.
updates.whyCare: For teams building vision-driven automation or robotics, the release adds a candidate model for work that spans perception, spatial reasoning, and code generation. The published benchmark and robotics trial are Google-reported results, so enterprise suitability still depends on workload-specific evaluation.
updates.before: Teams evaluating frontier models had no access to Gemini 4 Argon or evidence of its stated physical-reasoning and video-to-simulation capabilities.
updates.after: Developers and enterprises can evaluate Gemini 4 Argon for complex reasoning and embodied-AI use cases, alongside existing proprietary and open-weight model options.
updates.learn: Test the model on representative video, spatial-reasoning, and action-generation tasks; compare quality, latency, cost, and operational controls with alternative frontier and open models rather than generalizing from a vendor benchmark or demonstration.

sources.name: Google AI Blog - Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems

updates.architectureImplication: Treat Gemini 4 Argon as an additional model candidate for video-grounded and spatial workflows, and validate its performance and serving economics against existing model choices before making it a dependency.

updates.title: AWS Agent Registry adds schema-validated metadata for governed discovery
updates.whatChanged: AWS added registry-defined custom metadata schemas for agents, MCP servers, skills, gateways, and other records. Organizations can require common or type-specific fields such as owner, data classification, review status, or model family; the registry validates values on create and update and supports filtering by those fields in the console, CLI, SDKs, and MCP endpoint.
updates.whyCare: Teams managing large agent and tool inventories can encode ownership and review requirements directly in the catalog and use consistent fields for discovery, instead of relying only on names, descriptions, or a separate tracking system.
updates.before: Registry records relied on names and descriptions without organization-defined, schema-validated fields for governance and filtering.
updates.after: Administrators can define reusable common and record-type schemas, enforce required fields and allowed values, and filter registry results by custom metadata.
updates.learn: Define a small shared metadata schema for ownership, classification, and lifecycle status, then check that registry coverage and required-field policies match separate authorization, approval, and audit controls.

sources.name: AWS What's New - AWS Agent Registry now supports custom metadata for registry records
AWS Documentation - Define a custom metadata schema

updates.architectureImplication: Use registry metadata to provide a structured governance and discovery layer for agent resources, while keeping execution authorization and policy enforcement in the agent runtime and connected services.

updates.title: LangChain packages an open, model-agnostic deployment path for persistent agents
updates.whatChanged: LangChain launched Deep Agents deploy in beta, bundling deployment of its open-source agent harness with a horizontally scalable LangSmith Deployment server. The deployment includes agent APIs for MCP, A2A, human-in-the-loop controls, and memory; it supports multiple model and sandbox providers, and LangChain says deployments can be self-hosted so teams retain control of agent memory.
updates.whyCare: This gives teams an alternative to building their own runtime around an open harness or adopting a provider-specific managed agent. Portability now depends on more than model APIs: the agent harness, accumulated memory, tools, and runtime all affect switching costs.
updates.before: Teams either operated their own orchestration, memory, sandbox, and server infrastructure around open agent frameworks, or adopted managed runtimes that bundle those pieces behind provider-specific APIs.
updates.after: A beta deployment command packages an open-source, model-agnostic harness with managed or self-hostable serving, plus interoperable agent endpoints and optional sandbox integrations.
updates.learn: Compare the convenience of a bundled runtime with self-hosting and other managed options such as Claude Managed Agents or Bedrock AgentCore. Test model and sandbox portability, memory export and ownership, tenancy isolation, human approvals, and beta reliability before committing production state.

sources.name: LangChain - Deep Agents Deploy: an open alternative to Claude Managed Agents
LangChain documentation - Managed Deep Agents

updates.architectureImplication: Treat harness, runtime, memory, and sandbox as separate portability and governance decisions. An open harness and self-hostable deployment can reduce dependence on a single agent platform, but verify data ownership, isolation, controls, and service maturity rather than assuming model agnosticism alone prevents lock-in.

updates.title: GitHub Copilot HydraFusion drafts and reviews with several models per task
updates.whatChanged: GitHub updated HydraFusion, its research-preview Copilot orchestrator. Cascade judges a draft and asks a stronger model for a repair only when needed. Critique runs models in parallel to inspect the work. Each model call is billed at its standard rate.
updates.whyCare: Teams get draft-and-review patterns without building their own harness, though multi-pass work costs more credits and time.
updates.before: Teams picked one model, or built escalation and review workflows into their own agent harness.
updates.after: Copilot can pick one model, a judged cascade or parallel critique for each task.
updates.learn: Compare it with single-model use on real coding tasks. Track accepted changes, regressions, latency and credits. Keep it out of critical workflows while in preview.

sources.name: GitHub Changelog - HydraFusion updates and new Max option
GitHub documentation - Using HydraFusion

updates.architectureImplication: Choose orchestration per workload based on quality and cost. The preview has no SLA.

updates.title: AWS adds Meta Muse Spark Open to SageMaker JumpStart for in-account deployment
updates.whatChanged: AWS made Meta's Muse Spark Open available in SageMaker JumpStart in BF16 and NVFP4 variants. The 816B-parameter model has 42B active parameters, a 1M-token context window and text, image, document, audio and video input. It launches in two US East Regions.
updates.whyCare: Teams can test a large open-weight model on private code and media without sending data to a third-party API.
updates.before: Teams needed another deployment route to run Muse Spark Open on AWS.
updates.after: Teams can deploy it as a SageMaker endpoint in their own account with VPC, KMS encryption and network isolation.
updates.learn: Benchmark both variants on your tasks. Check the license, quotas and cost, since the endpoint bills on large GPU instances while active.

sources.name: AWS Machine Learning Blog - Meta's Muse Spark Open now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart

updates.architectureImplication: Weigh open-weight control against hosted APIs. Size for the full model memory and enforce license, network and cost controls.

updates.title: GitHub retires three Copilot models on 16 November 2026
updates.whatChanged: GitHub will deprecate Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Terra across Copilot on 16 November 2026. It recommends Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol or GPT-6 Luna as replacements, enabled automatically under default model policies.
updates.whyCare: Teams using these models have a fixed migration deadline and need to test the replacements first.
updates.before: The three models were available across supported Copilot experiences.
updates.after: They disappear from most Copilot experiences after 16 November. Opus 4.8 stays for annual individual plans.
updates.learn: List where you use these models. Test the replacements on real tasks and check your model policies before the deadline.

sources.name: GitHub Changelog - Upcoming deprecation of selected GitHub Copilot models in mid-November
GitHub Docs - Supported AI models in GitHub Copilot

updates.architectureImplication: Treat hosted models as versioned dependencies. Keep evaluations and a migration path ready for retirements.

updates.title: GitHub enforces license policy on new dependencies, including those added by agents
updates.whatChanged: GitHub made open source license compliance generally available for Enterprise Cloud with Code Security. Rulesets can block merges until new dependencies meet license policy. A new API lets coding agents check a package before they add it.
updates.whyCare: Coding agents add dependencies quickly, so license checks need to happen when they choose a package and again at merge.
updates.before: Pull request checks existed, but agents had no generally available API to check a package against policy.
updates.after: Agents can check packages through the API, and rulesets enforce policy before merge.
updates.learn: Connect your coding agents to the package check. Keep the required merge check as the final gate.

sources.name: GitHub Changelog - Open source license compliance generally available
GitHub Docs - About open source license compliance

updates.architectureImplication: Check license policy at package selection and enforce it again at merge. Audit exceptions.

updates.title: Reflection releases Beam, an open coding model you can run on AWS
updates.whatChanged: Reflection released Beam 1.0, an open-weight coding model with 501B total and 23B active parameters and a reported 1M-token context, under Apache 2.0. AWS offers it through SageMaker JumpStart and HyperPod in two US East Regions.
updates.whyCare: You can now run a coding model for agents inside your own AWS account, under a license that allows commercial use.
updates.before: Teams had to assemble serving for other open coding models themselves, and Beam was not yet available.
updates.after: Teams can deploy Beam through SageMaker JumpStart or HyperPod, or run the weights themselves.
updates.learn: Test Beam on your own agent tasks before you trust its benchmarks. Plan memory for all 501B parameters. Check which regions offer it.

sources.name: Hugging Face Blog - Welcome Beam: a 501B open model you can own, customize, and scale
AWS Machine Learning Blog - Introducing Reflection Beam, an open-weight model for agentic coding on AWS
AWS What's New - Beam model by Reflection is now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart and AWS Trainium

updates.architectureImplication: Compare self-hosting Beam with hosted coding models on quality, serving footprint and cost.

updates.title: Anthropic expands Claude's context window to 100K tokens
updates.whatChanged: Anthropic raised Claude's context window from 9K to 100K tokens, about 75,000 words.
updates.whyCare: Teams could put whole documents into one prompt for the first time at this scale.
updates.before: Most models held a few thousand tokens, so long documents had to be split or summarised first.
updates.after: A single request could hold a long report, contract or codebase section.
updates.learn: Compare long context with retrieval on your own documents. Measure cost and accuracy for each.

sources.name: Anthropic - Introducing 100K context windows

updates.architectureImplication: Long context became a design option next to retrieval. Choose per use case based on cost, latency and accuracy.

updates.title: Meta releases Llama 2 free for research and commercial use
updates.whatChanged: Meta released Llama 2 with model weights that companies could download and use commercially, together with Microsoft as a launch partner.
updates.whyCare: Companies could run a capable model on their own infrastructure under a license that allowed business use.
updates.before: Strong models were mostly available only through hosted APIs, and open models were limited or research-only.
updates.after: Teams could self-host, fine-tune and control a capable model.
updates.learn: Check the license terms for your use case. Plan for hosting, updates and safety controls you now own.

sources.name: Meta - Meta and Microsoft Introduce the Next Generation of Llama

updates.architectureImplication: Self-hosted models became a real option for data control and cost. Teams take on serving, scaling and model updates.

updates.title: OWASP publishes the first Top 10 risks for LLM applications
updates.whatChanged: OWASP published version 1.0 of its Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications. It lists the main risks, such as prompt injection and insecure output handling.
updates.whyCare: Security teams got a shared list to review LLM applications against.
updates.before: Teams had no common reference for LLM-specific security risks.
updates.after: Reviews, threat models and vendor questionnaires could point to one public list.
updates.learn: Review your application against the current version of the list. Add the relevant risks to your threat model.

sources.name: OWASP - Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications
SD Times - OWASP releases Top 10 list for LLMs

updates.architectureImplication: Treat model input and output as untrusted. Add controls for prompt injection, output handling and excessive agent permissions.
updates.verificationNote: The OWASP page shows no release date. Date from SD Times coverage published 2 August 2023.

updates.title: Microsoft makes Microsoft 365 Copilot generally available to enterprises
updates.whatChanged: Microsoft made Copilot for Microsoft 365 generally available to enterprise customers on 1 November 2023, inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams.
updates.whyCare: GenAI moved into the office software most companies already use, with access tied to existing company data and permissions.
updates.before: Most GenAI use at work happened in separate chat tools.
updates.after: Employees could use GenAI inside their daily applications, grounded in company files and email.
updates.learn: Check how your data permissions apply when an assistant can read across files and email. Fix oversharing before rollout.

sources.name: Microsoft - Announcing Microsoft 365 Copilot general availability and Microsoft 365 Chat

updates.architectureImplication: Existing access controls became the boundary for what AI can see. Data governance became a prerequisite for rollout.

updates.title: OpenAI launches the Assistants API and GPT-4 Turbo with 128K context
updates.whatChanged: At DevDay, OpenAI announced GPT-4 Turbo with a 128K context window, JSON mode, and the Assistants API with threads, retrieval and code execution.
updates.whyCare: Developers could build assistants that keep state and use tools without running that infrastructure themselves.
updates.before: Developers stored conversation state, retrieval and tool loops in their own code.
updates.after: The platform could hold threads, files and tool calls for them.
updates.learn: Decide which state you want the vendor to hold. Check how to export it if you change vendors.

sources.name: OpenAI - New models and developer products announced at DevDay

updates.architectureImplication: State and tool orchestration could move into the vendor platform. This trades build effort for portability.

updates.title: EU AI Act enters into force
updates.whatChanged: The EU AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024. Its rules apply in stages over the following years.
updates.whyCare: Teams that build or use AI in the EU now have legal duties that depend on the risk level of each use case.
updates.before: No broad law set rules for how AI systems are built and used in the EU.
updates.after: Providers and deployers must classify use cases by risk and meet the duties for each level.
updates.learn: List your AI use cases and classify them by risk. Track which obligations apply on which date.

sources.name: European Commission - AI Act enters into force

updates.architectureImplication: Plan for documentation, logging, human oversight and transparency features as part of the design.

updates.title: OpenAI makes model output follow a developer's JSON schema
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI introduced Structured Outputs in the API. Model outputs now reliably follow a JSON Schema the developer supplies.
updates.whyCare: Systems that pass model output to other code can rely on its shape.
updates.before: Developers asked for JSON in the prompt, then validated and retried when the output broke.
updates.after: The API guarantees the output matches the schema.
updates.learn: Define schemas for every model output that other code reads. Remove retry logic that only fixed format errors.

sources.name: OpenAI - Introducing Structured Outputs in the API

updates.architectureImplication: Model output can feed other systems directly. Validation still matters for content, though format errors drop away.

updates.title: Anthropic introduces prompt caching for long, repeated context
updates.whatChanged: Anthropic launched prompt caching for Claude. Reusing a cached prompt prefix cuts cost by up to 90% and latency by up to 85% for long prompts.
updates.whyCare: Long system prompts, documents and tool definitions became cheap to resend on every call.
updates.before: Every request paid full price for the whole prompt, even when most of it repeated.
updates.after: Repeated context costs a fraction of the normal input price.
updates.learn: Put stable content at the start of the prompt and changing content at the end. Measure your cache hit rate.

sources.name: Anthropic - Prompt caching with Claude
SD Times - Anthropic introduces prompt caching

updates.architectureImplication: Prompt structure became a cost lever. Agents and long-context designs got much cheaper to run.
updates.verificationNote: Anthropic's page now shows a later republish date. Launch date confirmed by news coverage from 14 August 2024.

updates.title: Anthropic launches Claude Code, an agentic coding tool for the terminal
updates.whatChanged: Anthropic released Claude Code in limited research preview with Claude 3.7 Sonnet. Developers can hand off engineering tasks from their terminal.
updates.whyCare: Coding assistants started to act on a codebase, editing files and running commands.
updates.before: Coding assistants mostly suggested code inside an editor for a developer to accept.
updates.after: An agent could carry out multi-step engineering tasks under a developer's direction.
updates.learn: Set clear permissions for what a coding agent may run. Review its changes like any other contributor's.

sources.name: Anthropic - Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Claude Code

updates.architectureImplication: Developer machines and repositories became places where agents act. Permissions and review gates matter.

updates.title: OpenAI launches Codex, a cloud coding agent that works on tasks in parallel
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI introduced Codex as a cloud-based software engineering agent that can work on many tasks in parallel.
updates.whyCare: Coding agents moved off the developer's machine and into managed cloud sandboxes.
updates.before: Coding agents ran one task at a time on a developer's machine.
updates.after: Teams could queue several coding tasks to agents running in the cloud.
updates.learn: Decide which repositories and secrets a cloud agent may access. Track the cost and quality of agent work.

sources.name: OpenAI - Introducing Codex

updates.architectureImplication: Agent work became something you can run in parallel and in the cloud. Sandboxes, secrets and review queues became part of the design.

updates.title: EU AI Act rules for general-purpose AI models start to apply
updates.whatChanged: From 2 August 2025, providers of general-purpose AI models in the EU must meet transparency and copyright duties under the AI Act.
updates.whyCare: Model providers must now document their models, which gives teams more information when they choose one.
updates.before: Model providers had no legal duty in the EU to document training data or model capabilities.
updates.after: Providers must publish documentation and a summary of training content.
updates.learn: Ask model vendors for their AI Act documentation. Use it in your model selection and risk records.

sources.name: European Commission - General-purpose AI obligations under the AI Act

updates.architectureImplication: Use vendor documentation when you select a model and keep it in your risk records.

updates.title: OpenAI releases gpt-oss, its first open-weight models since 2019
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI released gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b under the Apache 2.0 license.
updates.whyCare: A leading model lab now offered open weights, so teams could self-host models from the same vendor they use through an API.
updates.before: OpenAI models were available only through hosted services.
updates.after: Teams could run OpenAI reasoning models on their own infrastructure.
updates.learn: Test the open models against your hosted model on the same tasks. Compare total cost, including serving.

sources.name: OpenAI - Introducing gpt-oss

updates.architectureImplication: Mixed designs became easier: hosted models for some tasks, self-hosted open weights for sensitive or high-volume ones.

updates.title: OpenAI releases GPT-5 with a router between fast and deep reasoning
updates.whatChanged: OpenAI released GPT-5 as the new default in ChatGPT. A router picks a quick model or a deeper reasoning model for each request.
updates.whyCare: Choosing between a fast model and a reasoning model became something the system can decide per request.
updates.before: Users and developers picked a reasoning or non-reasoning model themselves.
updates.after: One entry point routes each request to the right level of reasoning.
updates.learn: Test how routing affects your cost and latency. Pin a model version where you need predictable behaviour.

sources.name: OpenAI - Introducing GPT-5

updates.architectureImplication: Routing between model tiers became a standard design pattern, inside vendor products and in your own systems.

updates.title: Anthropic adds context editing and a memory tool for long-running agents
updates.whatChanged: Anthropic launched context editing, which clears stale tool results as the context fills, and a memory tool that stores information in files outside the context. OpenAI added compaction in December 2025 and Anthropic a Compaction API in February 2026.
updates.whyCare: Agents can now run far longer than one context window because the platform manages what stays in context.
updates.before: Developers trimmed, summarised and stored agent context with their own code.
updates.after: Major platforms offer context editing, memory and compaction as built-in features.
updates.learn: Test how your agent behaves when old context is cleared or compacted. Decide what must go to durable memory.

sources.name: Anthropic - Managing context on the Claude Developer Platform
OpenAI - API changelog (compaction, 11 December 2025)
Anthropic - Claude Platform release notes (Compaction API, 5 February 2026)

updates.architectureImplication: Context became a managed resource. Design what lives in the window, what goes to memory and what gets summarised.

updates.title: Linux Foundation forms the Agentic AI Foundation for MCP, goose and AGENTS.md
updates.whatChanged: The Linux Foundation announced the Agentic AI Foundation, with the Model Context Protocol, goose and AGENTS.md as founding projects.
updates.whyCare: Key agent standards moved under neutral governance, which lowers the risk of building on them.
updates.before: MCP and related agent standards were led by single companies.
updates.after: A vendor-neutral foundation governs them.
updates.learn: Prefer standards with neutral governance for long-lived integrations. Track the foundation's specification releases.

sources.name: Linux Foundation - Announces the formation of the Agentic AI Foundation

updates.architectureImplication: MCP-based integrations became a safer long-term bet for tool and data connections.

updates.title: Anthropic publishes Agent Skills as an open standard
updates.whatChanged: Anthropic published the Agent Skills specification as an open standard at agentskills.io. OpenAI added Skills support to its Responses API in February 2026.
updates.whyCare: Teams can package instructions, scripts and resources for agents once and use them across vendors.
updates.before: Each agent platform had its own way to package reusable know-how.
updates.after: A shared format works across at least two major platforms.
updates.learn: Package repeated agent procedures as skills. Keep them in version control like code.

sources.name: Anthropic - Organization skills and directory
OpenAI - API changelog (Skills in the Responses API, 10 February 2026)

updates.architectureImplication: Agent know-how became a portable asset that teams can version, review and share.

updates.title: EU AI Act transparency rules start to apply
updates.whatChanged: From 2 August 2026, AI-generated content such as deepfakes must be labelled, and users must be told when they interact with an AI system such as a chatbot.
updates.whyCare: Customer-facing AI in the EU now needs disclosure and content labelling built in.
updates.before: Disclosure and labelling were voluntary in most products.
updates.after: Providers and deployers in the EU must disclose AI interaction and label AI-generated content.
updates.learn: Check every customer-facing AI feature for disclosure. Add labels or metadata to generated media.

sources.name: European Commission - Safer and more transparent AI

updates.architectureImplication: Disclosure and content labelling became product requirements for AI features used in the EU.

updates.title: GitHub lets Copilot span repositories in Slack and Teams
updates.whatChanged: GitHub says Copilot in Slack and Microsoft Teams now supports one conversation across multiple repositories. Users can create issues, open pull requests, and investigate bugs across repositories in that conversation. The update adds shared Slack thread context, easier repository switching, mentions anywhere in a message, and reliability improvements.
updates.whyCare: You can bring code and discussion context together across repositories in Slack or Teams. Teams coordinating work across services can handle cross-repository tasks in one agent conversation, with repository permissions and pull request review as controls.
updates.before: GitHub in Slack and Teams handled one repository per conversation. Teams had to start separate conversations or transfer context to investigate and change multiple repositories.
updates.after: GitHub in Slack and Teams now lets one conversation span repositories. Users can investigate bugs, create issues, and open pull requests across them.
updates.learn: Test cross-repository tasks in representative Slack and Teams workflows. Review which repositories your users can access and preserve human review before merging agent-generated changes.

sources.name: GitHub Changelog - Multi-repository support and other improvements for GitHub in Slack and Teams

updates.architectureImplication: Teams can start cross-repository agent tasks in Slack and Teams and carry thread context into code work. Keep repository access scoped, and retain pull request checks and human review.

overallDirection.title: From assistants to agents and automated knowledge work
overallDirection.summary: The broad direction is toward systems that reason longer, use tools, act across software, and take on larger portions of real work. Model capability still matters, but the architectural bottleneck is moving toward reliable autonomy and integration.
overallDirection.destination: Increasingly general AI systems that can perform broad cognitive work, research, and operations under human direction. This is a direction of travel, not a guaranteed end state.
overallDirection.constraint: Alignment, monitoring, permissions, security, reliability, and preserving meaningful human control as systems become more autonomous.
